vulnerability: Unrestricted mint amount for whitelisted addresses
reason: The function only checks _numberMinted(msg.sender) < 1 to limit each address to one mint transaction, but the user-supplied chosenAmount is not restricted to 1. A whitelisted attacker can pass the maximum remaining public supply (e.g., maxsupply - reserve - totalSupply()) and mint all available public tokens in a single transaction. This deprives other whitelisted users and allows the attacker to acquire a large supply for free, which can be sold or used to manipulate the NFT market.

vulnerability: Missing total supply cap check allows owner to mint beyond maxsupply
reason: The function only ensures quantity <= reserve and decrements reserve. It does not check totalSupply() + quantity <= maxsupply. Because setReserve can be called repeatedly to reset reserve to any value up to maxsupply, the owner can repeatedly call setReserve(maxsupply) and mintReservedTokens(maxsupply) to mint an unbounded number of tokens. Even without resetting, after public minting has occurred, increasing reserve via setReserve allows the owner to mint more than the original reserve, exceeding maxsupply. This breaks the supply cap and allows the owner to dilute the collection arbitrarily.

vulnerability: Reserve can be arbitrarily reset, enabling supply cap bypass and public mint DoS
reason: setReserve can be called at any time by the owner and only checks _reserve <= maxsupply. It does not consider the current total supply or the amount already minted. An owner can set reserve = maxsupply to make maxsupply - reserve = 0, completely disabling WhiteListMint. More critically, combined with mintReservedTokens, the ability to reset reserve after it has been consumed allows the owner to mint unlimited tokens in multiple iterations. This is a severe centralization risk and a direct violation of the advertised maximum supply.
